Welcome to the official API reference for the Trading 212 Public API!
This guide provides all the information you need to start building your
own trading applications and integrations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#  {#section/General-Information .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/General-Information){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/General-Information"}General Information

This API is currently in **beta** and is under active development.
We\'re continuously adding new features and improvements, and we welcome
your feedback.

###  {#section/general-information/Only-for-Invest-and-Stocks-ISA .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/general-information/Only-for-Invest-and-Stocks-ISA){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/general-information/Only-for-Invest-and-Stocks-ISA"}Only
for Invest and Stocks ISA

The API described here is enabled and usable only for **Invest and
Stocks ISA** account types.

###  {#section/general-information/API-Environments .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/general-information/API-Environments){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/general-information/API-Environments"}API
Environments

We provide two distinct environments for development and trading:

- **Paper Trading (Demo):** `https://demo.trading212.com/api/v0`

- **Live Trading (Real Money):** `https://live.trading212.com/api/v0`

You can test your applications extensively in the paper trading
environment without risking real funds before moving to live trading.

###  {#section/general-information/API-Limitations .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/general-information/API-Limitations){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/general-information/API-Limitations"}⚠️ API
Limitations

Please be aware of the following limitations for any order placement:

- **Supported account types:** The Trading 212 Public API is enabled and
  usable only for **Invest and Stocks ISA** account types.

- **Order execution:** Orders can be executed only in the **primary
  account currency**

- **Multi-currency:** Multi-currency accounts are not currently
  supported through the API. Meaning your account, position and result
  values in the responses will be in the primary account currency.

###  {#section/general-information/Key-Concepts .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/general-information/Key-Concepts){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/general-information/Key-Concepts"}Key
Concepts

- **Authentication:** Every request to the API must be authenticated
  using a secure key pair. See the **Authentication** section below for
  details.

- **Rate Limiting:** All API calls are subject to rate limits to ensure
  fair usage and stability. See the **Rate Limiting** section for a full
  explanation.

- **IP Restrictions:** For enhanced security, you can optionally
  restrict your API keys to a specific set of IP addresses from within
  your Trading 212 account settings.

- **Selling Orders:** To execute a sell order, you must provide a
  **negative** value for the `quantity` parameter (e.g., `-10.5`). This
  is a core convention of the API.


------------------------------------------------------------------------

##  {#section/general-information/Quickstart .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/general-information/Quickstart){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/general-information/Quickstart"}Quickstart

This simple example shows you how to retrieve your account\'s cash
balance.

First, you must generate your API keys from within the Trading 212 app.
For detailed instructions, please visit our Help Centre:

- [**How to get your Trading 212 API
  key**](https://helpcentre.trading212.com/hc/en-us/articles/14584770928157-Trading-212-API-key)

Once you have your **API Key** and **API Secret**, you can make your
first call using `cURL`:

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.WarningSquareIcon-sc-1qfipv9-0
.gLsLkL}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.CopyIcon-sc-1n8wc2v-0
.dmyhrq}

``` {.CodeBlockContainer__CodeBlockContainerComponent-sc-wgyn12-0 .bfCLHN testid="source-code" tabindex="0" component-name="CodeBlock/CodeBlockContainer"}

# Step 1: Replace with your actual credentials and Base64-encode them.

# The `-n` is important as it prevents adding a newline character.

CREDENTIALS=$(echo -n "<YOUR_API_KEY>:<YOUR_API_SECRET>" | base64)


# Step 2: Make the API call to the live environment using the encoded
credentials.

curl -X GET "https://live.trading212.com/api/v0/equity/account/cash" \
 -H "Authorization: Basic $CREDENTIALS"
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

#  {#section/Authentication .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/Authentication){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/Authentication"}Authentication

The API uses a secure key pair for authentication on every request. You
must provide your **API Key** as the username and your **API Secret** as
the password, formatted as an HTTP Basic Authentication header.

The `Authorization` header is constructed by Base64-encoding your
`API_KEY:API_SECRET` string and prepending it with `Basic `.

###  {#section/authentication/Building-the-Authorization-Header .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/authentication/Building-the-Authorization-Header){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/authentication/Building-the-Authorization-Header"}Building
the Authorization Header

Here are examples of how to generate the required value in different
environments.

**Linux or macOS (Terminal)**

You can use the `echo` and `base64` commands. Remember to use the `-n`
flag with `echo` to prevent it from adding a trailing newline, which
would invalidate the credential string.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.WarningSquareIcon-sc-1qfipv9-0
.gLsLkL}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.CopyIcon-sc-1n8wc2v-0
.dmyhrq}

``` {.CodeBlockContainer__CodeBlockContainerComponent-sc-wgyn12-0 .bfCLHN testid="source-code" tabindex="0" component-name="CodeBlock/CodeBlockContainer"}

# This command outputs the required Base64-encoded string for your header.

echo -n "<YOUR_API_KEY>:<YOUR_API_SECRET>" | base64
```

**Python**

This simple snippet shows how to generate the full header value.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.WarningSquareIcon-sc-1qfipv9-0
.gLsLkL}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.CopyIcon-sc-1n8wc2v-0
.dmyhrq}

``` {.CodeBlockContainer__CodeBlockContainerComponent-sc-wgyn12-0 .bfCLHN testid="source-code" tabindex="0" component-name="CodeBlock/CodeBlockContainer"}



# 1. Your credentials

api_key = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"

api_secret = "<YOUR_API_SECRET>"


# 2. Combine them into a single string

credentials_string = f"{api_key}:{api_secret}"


# 3. Encode the string to bytes, then Base64 encode it

encoded_credentials =
base64.b64encode(credentials_string.encode('utf-8')).decode('utf-8')


# 4. The final header value

auth_header = f"Basic {encoded_credentials}"


print(auth_header)
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

#  {#section/Rate-Limiting .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/Rate-Limiting){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/Rate-Limiting"}Rate Limiting

To ensure high performance and fair access for all users, all API
endpoints are subject to rate limiting.

> **IMPORTANT NOTE:** All rate limits are applied on a per-account
> basis, regardless of which API key is used or which IP address the
> request originates from.

Specific rate limits are detailed in the reference for each endpoint.

###  {#section/rate-limiting/Response-Headers .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/rate-limiting/Response-Headers){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/rate-limiting/Response-Headers"}Response
Headers

Every API response includes the following headers to help you manage
your request frequency and avoid hitting limits.

- `x-ratelimit-limit`: The total number of requests allowed in the
  current time period.

- `x-ratelimit-period`: The duration of the time period in seconds.

- `x-ratelimit-remaining`: The number of requests you have left in the
  current period.

- `x-ratelimit-reset`: A Unix timestamp indicating the exact time when
  the limit will be fully reset.

- `x-ratelimit-used`: The number of requests you have already made in
  the current period.

###  {#section/rate-limiting/How-It-Works .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/rate-limiting/How-It-Works){.anchor
.before aria-label="link  to section/rate-limiting/How-It-Works"}How It
Works

The rate limiter allows for requests to be made in bursts. For example,
an endpoint with a limit of `50 requests per 1 minute` does **not**
strictly mean you can only make one request every 1.2 seconds. Instead,
you could:

- Make a burst of all 50 requests in the first 5 seconds of a minute.
  You would then need to wait for the reset time indicated by the
  `x-ratelimit-reset` header before making more requests.

- Pace your requests evenly, for example, by making one call every 1.2
  seconds, ensuring you always stay within the limit.

###  {#section/rate-limiting/Function-Specific-Limits .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/rate-limiting/Function-Specific-Limits){.anchor
.before
aria-label="link  to section/rate-limiting/Function-Specific-Limits"}Function-Specific
Limits

In addition to the general rate limits on HTTP calls, some actions have
their own functional limits. For example, there is a maximum of **50
pending orders** allowed per ticker, per account.

#  {#section/Pagination .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/Pagination){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/Pagination"}Pagination

All list endpoints in the API that return a collection of items (such as
historical orders, dividends, and transactions) use **cursor-based
pagination** to handle large data sets.

###  {#section/pagination/Parameters .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/pagination/Parameters){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/pagination/Parameters"}Parameters

- **`limit`** (integer): Specifies the maximum number of items to return
  in a single request.
  - **Default:** 20
  - **Maximum:** 50
- **`cursor`** (string \| number): A pointer to a specific item in the
  dataset. This tells the API where to start the next page of results.

###  {#section/pagination/How-to-Paginate .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/pagination/How-to-Paginate){.anchor
.before aria-label="link  to section/pagination/How-to-Paginate"}How to
Paginate

The easiest way to paginate is by using the `nextPagePath` field
returned in the response.

1.  Make your initial request to a list endpoint (e.g.,
    `/api/v0/equity/history/orders`) with an optional `limit` parameter.
    Do not include a `cursor`.
2.  The API will return a response object. This object will contain a
    list of `items` and a `nextPagePath` field.
3.  If the `nextPagePath` field is `null`, you have reached the end of
    the data, and there are no more pages.
4.  If `nextPagePath` is not `null`, **use the entire string value of
    `nextPagePath`** as the path for your next request. This string
    contains all the necessary parameters (like `limit` and `cursor`) to
    get the next page.
5.  Repeat this process until `nextPagePath` is `null`.

###  {#section/pagination/Example .heading-anchor .md component-name="Markdoc/Heading/Heading"}

[![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0
.bMrZKW}](dividends.html#section/pagination/Example){.anchor .before
aria-label="link  to section/pagination/Example"}Example

Here is a step-by-step example of fetching all transactions, 2 at a
time.

**Request 1: Get the first page**

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.WarningSquareIcon-sc-1qfipv9-0
.gLsLkL}

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.CopyIcon-sc-1n8wc2v-0
.dmyhrq}

#### [![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,){.LinkIcon-sc-q8trda-0 .cTsuhK}](getreports.html#historical-events/getreports/request){#historical-events/getreports/request .sc-aXZVg .gtwLYJ .sc-gEvEer .hIFHmR aria-label="link to /historical-events/getreports#historical-events/getreports/request"}Request {#request-1 .sc-hTUWRQ .gtWNd}

Retrieves a list of all requested CSV reports and their current status.

**Asynchronous Workflow:**

1.  Call `POST /history/exports` to request a report. You will receive a
    `reportId`.

2.  Periodically call this endpoint (`GET /history/exports`) to check
    the `status` of the report corresponding to your `reportId`.

3.  Once the status is `Finished`, the `downloadLink` field will contain
    a URL to download the CSV file.

**Rate limit:** 1 req / 1m0s

data. This is an asynchronous operation. The response will include a

process using the `GET /history/exports` endpoint.
